title: docs-digger output
description: overlunky's Lua API as docs-digger extracts it. Optional fields are left out when empty, false or default. C++ types are kept as written; turning them into Lua names is up to the output stage. Every object lists all its fields: a field not described here is an error.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema. Raised with every change to the fields or their meaning.

functions.description: Lua functions bound with `root["a"]["name"] = <callable>` or documented by a commented-out binding, ordered by owner, name and source.

values.description: Lua values that are not functions (`lua["players"] = ...`), ordered like functions.

usertypes.description: C++ types exposed with `new_usertype<T>("Name", ...)`, ordered by Lua name.

enums.description: Lua tables of named constants (`create_named_table`, `new_enum`, the runtime enum file), ordered by name.

aliases.description: Typedef and `using` names under the root that some Lua-visible type is written with, ordered by name.

script_callbacks.description: Documented globals that scripts define and C++ reads (`on_frame`), ordered by name.

global_variables.description: Names of the documented values bound on the Lua state (`state`, `players`); their types are in `values`.

events.description: Callbacks of enum-keyed dispatches: one per key of the selecting enum (`ON.FRAME`, `THEME_OVERRIDE.SPAWN_LEVEL`), ordered by storage, table and key.

file.description: Path relative to the --root directory, '/' separated.

line.description: 1-based line of the entity's first token.

column.description: 1-based column, telling several bindings on one line apart.

Doc.description: Lines of the `///` comment without the markers. Leading `NoDoc` / `Deprecated` lines and a `Group:` line are taken out (see `nodoc`, `deprecated`, `group`); `Returns`, `Default`, `note:` and `Warning:` stay in the text.

NoDoc.description: `/// NoDoc`: exists in Lua but is kept out of the documentation.

Deprecated.description: `/// Deprecated`: still works; documented apart with its replacement.

Owner.description: Table keys before the name (`["TYPE_MAP"]` for `lua["TYPE_MAP"]["x"]`); left out for globals.

Root.description: Source text of the root when it is neither the Lua state nor an environment (a local `sol::table`); left out otherwise.

Type.description: One C++ type and what it means in Lua.

spelling.description: As written in the source, typedef names kept (`std::vector<ENT_TYPE>`).

canonical.description: Fully resolved type; only present when it differs from the spelling.

kind.description: Lua meaning. `lua_object`: a sol2 handle to any Lua value (object, table, userdata, ...). `variadic`: any number of values. `nil`: an assignment that removes a value. `unknown`: not classified (the parity report lists these; doc-only entries are always unknown).

inner.description: Container elements, optional payload, pointee, tuple members, or the parameters of a `function` kind.

returns.description: Return types of a `function` kind with a known signature (`std::function`).

nullable.description: Lua may pass or get nil here (optional, raw pointer, `sol::object`).

hidden.description: Injected by sol2 (`sol::this_state`, ...): not a Lua-visible parameter.

lua.description: The type in LuaLS notation, built from the facts above (P16): `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `string`, `nil`; usertype, enum table and alias names; `T?` for nullable pointers and optionals; `T[]` and `table<K, V>` for containers; `[A, B]` for tuples inside containers; `fun(p1: A): R` for `std::function`, `function` for other callables; `table`, `userdata` or `any` for sol2 handles; `any` for variadic values (the parameter itself is `...`). --lua-types (config/lua_types.json) names what the facts cannot. Text-only types are converted word by word.

Param.description: A parameter of a bound C++ function, or an argument a Lua callback receives.

name.description: Name in the C++ declaration; empty when unnamed.

omittable.description: Part of the trailing run of nullable parameters: a Lua call may leave it out.

binder.description: Callback arguments only: a value `make_safe_cb` adds in front of (`front`) or behind (`back`) the caller's arguments.

Callback.description: The Lua function a parameter receives: what it is called with, what it may return, and what nil means.

origin.description: How the signature was found: from a `std::function` type, `make_safe_cb<Sig>` binders, `handle_function<R>` on the parameter, a direct call, a stored callback dispatched elsewhere, an enum-keyed dispatch (signatures in `events`), a vtable hook, only the doc comment's `The callback signature is ...` prose, or not at all (`unresolved`).

params.description: Arguments the callback receives, binder values marked. Present unless unresolved or selected.

returns.description: Values the C++ side reads back; empty when the result is ignored. Present unless unresolved or selected.

nil_allowed.description: nil (or no return value) is accepted. Present unless unresolved or selected.

nil_meaning.description: What the C++ side does with nil (`ignored`, `treated as false`, `the original runs`, ...).

stored_in.description: Record field the callback is stored in (`ScreenCallback::func`), with ` in <container>` when known.

selector.description: Enum whose value selects the signature (`ON`); the signatures are in `events`.

unresolved.description: The pattern that stopped the search, when no signature was found in code.

prose.description: The `The callback signature is ...` text of the doc comment.

conflicts.description: Disagreements between dispatch sites, or between the code and the prose (doc fixes for overlunky).

source.description: Where the signature was read (the `make_safe_cb` or `handle_function` call).

Signature.description: One callable form: a lambda, a C++ function, or one member of a `sol::overload`.

params.description: Parameters in declaration order, hidden ones included.

returns.description: Values returned to Lua: empty for void, several for tuples and pairs.

cpp.description: Qualified name of the bound C++ function, or `lambda at <file>:<line>`; for doc-only entries the comment's text.

doc.description: Comment of the C++ declaration, for named functions.

self.description: Usertype members: the object is `this` of a C++ member function (`implicit`), or the first parameter (`first_param`).

group.description: Documentation section: the `/// Group: <name>` directive, else the table it is bound in (root and owner joined with '.'), else the first matching rule of --groups (config/groups.json), else that file's fallback, else the source file name without `_lua` (`spawn_lua.cpp` gives `spawn`).

overloads.description: All callable forms; several for `sol::overload`. Empty for `defined_in_lua`.

doc_only.description: Known only from a `///` block followed by a commented-out binding (`// lua["get_entity"] = [](uint32_t uid) -> Entity*{};`): written in Lua; types are text only (kind `unknown`).

defined_in_lua.description: `lua["printf"] = lua.safe_script(...)`: written in Lua, no C++ signature.

alias_of.description: `lua["a"] = lua["b"]`: the keys of the aliased function, whose overloads are copied here.

Value.description: A Lua value that is not a function.

type.description: Type of the assigned C++ expression.

doc_only.description: Known only from a commented-out binding; the type's spelling is the comment's text.

Member.description: One member of a usertype. A key bound twice appears twice (sol2 keeps the last).

name.description: Key in Lua; for meta functions the `sol::meta_function` name (`equal_to`).

kind.description: `field`: `&T::field`, read and written. `readonly`: `sol::readonly(&T::field)`. `property`: `sol::property(get[, set])`. `method`: a callable (lambda, member function, `sol::overload`, vtable hook). `value`: anything else.

source.description: The key argument or the `ut["k"] = ...` statement.

doc.description: Comment above the binding, or from a `/* Usertype // key // doc */` block.

cpp_doc.description: Comment of the bound C++ field, the field a getter reads, an autodoc hint, or the C++ member of the same name.

type.description: All kinds but `method`: field type, property type (getter result), or value type.

setter.description: Setter of a `property`; left out when read only.

Usertype.description: A C++ type exposed to Lua.

bases.description: C++ base classes from `sol::bases<...>`, as written.

group.description: Documentation group the type is listed under: the `/// Group: <name>` directive, else the first matching type rule of --groups (config/groups.json `types`), else that file's type fallback, else the source file name without `_lua`.

section.description: Part of the documentation that holds the group (`Entity types`), from the same rule or fallback; left out when it gives none.

members.description: Members from the `new_usertype` arguments, `ut["k"] = v`, `lua["Name"]["k"] = v` and vtable hooks, ordered by name and source.

EnumValue.description: One key of an enum table.

name.description: Key in Lua; empty for a commented-out hint such as `"", ...check [entities.txt]...`.

text.description: The value as written (`ON::LOGO`, `0x1`), or as the runtime file has it.

value.description: The value when it is an integer known at compile time (or in the runtime file), or a string.

doc.description: From a `/* ENUM // KEY // doc */` block.

origin.description: Left out for a pair written in code. `doc_comment`: a commented-out pair inside the call, an example of values added at runtime. `runtime_file`: from --runtime-enums (`lua_enums.txt`).

source.description: The key in the code; left out for runtime values.

Enum.description: A Lua table of named constants.

name.description: Name of the table in Lua.

values.description: Values ordered by key and source; a key may repeat with another origin.

source.description: The creating call; left out for tables only the runtime file knows (then `origin` is present).

origin.description: `runtime_file` for tables only the runtime file knows.

filled_at_runtime.description: Code also adds keys at runtime (`lua["ENT_TYPE"][name] = ...` in a loop).

function.description: C++ function the call is in (`load_unsafe_libraries` opens the unsafe ones).

ScriptCallback.description: A documented global that the script defines and C++ reads.

type.description: C++ type the value is read as (`sol::optional<sol::function>`).

Event.description: The Lua callback for one key of an enum-keyed dispatch.

stored_in.description: Record field the callbacks are stored in (`ScreenCallback::func`).

callback.description: Signature from the key's dispatch sites (merged), the generic dispatch, or unresolved.

generic.description: The key has no dispatch site of its own: the signature is the generic dispatch's.
